decisionsTitle: The calendar's period is in the address's path: the arrows, the selects and the swipe show the month again
decisionsSection:
**The owner, 2026-09-29 22:45**, with a screenshot of `/ro/calendar`'s controls («Luna: Septembrie», «Anul: 2026», «‹ Azi ›», «Lună | An», «Calendar | Listă»): «nu pot schimba luna din săgeți (deși se schimbă în query params) dar nu văd evenimentele din octombrie; de asemenea s-a stricat și la swipe pe telefon».

**The cause, measured.** Of the three suspects the brief named, it was none as stated and closest to the first: the page was right, the router never asked it.

- *Not the server.* On production, `curl /ro/calendar` answered the static page (`X-Vercel-Cache: HIT`, `X-Matched-Path: /[locale]/calendar`, «septembrie 2026») and `curl /ro/calendar?month=2026-10` the live twin (`X-Matched-Path: /[locale]/live/calendar`, `private, no-store`, «octombrie 2026», October's events in the HTML). The same on a local `yarn build && yarn start`. A direct link to October showed October.
- *Not the island.* Nothing on the client reads the query; the month is server HTML, and a soft navigation replaces it only if the router fetches it.
- *Not BR-V2.40 or the footer hotfix.* `git log -8 --stat -- 'src/app/[locale]/calendar'`: the compact head (2dcaa109) and the release commit changed a few `sx` lines. The break came with §549 (BR-V2.24, b52cae56), which made the bare calendar static and every other month a query the proxy rewrites to the twin.
- *The router answered from a prefetch.* A headless Chromium on production, from `/ro/evenimente`: the header's «Calendar» link prefetched `/ro/calendar` (`Next-Router-Segment-Prefetch: /_tree`), the click showed September, and › put `?month=2026-10` in the address, **sent no request**, and left September on screen; a second › went to `?month=2026-10` again, because the arrows on screen were still September's. From a direct load the first › worked, and the second showed September under `?month=2026-11`, once the header link's prefetch had arrived. Vercel answers that segment prefetch with the page's whole flight data (94 412 bytes, `X-Matched-Path: /[locale]/calendar.rsc`, `X-Nextjs-Prerender: 1`); `next start` answers it with the tree alone, which is why no local run and no end-to-end test ever saw it. Answering the prefetch the way Vercel does (a Playwright route) reproduced the owner's screen on a local build exactly; aborting the prefetch of the bare page made every arrow work. Next 16.3.4 says why in its own client: a static prefetch "never include[s] search params, so [it] can be reused across all possible search param values" (`segment-cache/vary-path.js`), and it "optimistically assume[s] that rewrites for the requested pathname do not vary on the search string" (`segment-cache/cache.js`). A static page cannot read its query, so to the router its copy answers every query; the proxy's rewrite by `?month=` is exactly what that assumption forbids.
- *The swipe* pushes the arrows' own addresses (§475), so it broke with them: the address changed out of sight and the month stayed.

**Decision.** A period lives in the path, never in the query:

- `/ro/calendar` is this month as a grid; `/ro/calendar/2026-10` October; `/ro/calendar/2026-10/list` October as a list; `/ro/calendar/2026` the year (a year has no layout). The same words in both languages, like `/calendar`. One route, `app/[locale]/calendar/[...period]/page.tsx`, renders the bare page's component with the segments; `events/domain/calendar-path.ts` reads and builds them (pure, tested). A malformed period, a year with a layout, a third segment or a period more than two years away is a 404 — the bound the selects and the old `?month=` had.
- Every control builds its address with `calendarAddress`: the arrows and so the swipe (`calendarStepHrefs`), «Azi», the two selects, «Lună», «An», «Calendar», «Listă» and the year's month headings. The bare path is used only for this month as a grid with nothing filtered; everything else spells its period, this month included.
- The filters stay in the query, on the period's own path: `/ro/calendar/2026-10?type=RACE` is the period's live twin (`live/calendar/[...period]/page.tsx`). The filter form's action and its chips always spell the period, even for this month, so no filtered address is a query on the bare path — the one address the header prefetches. Measured on a local build with Vercel's prefetch answer: a filter, › with it, clearing it and «Azi» all showed the period and the filter they named.
- The old addresses are answered by the proxy before anything renders: `?month=`, `?year=` and `?view=list` on the bare calendar are redirected to the same period's path, every other key kept and Next's `_rsc` dropped (`i18n/calendar-redirect.ts`), with the old readings (`?year=` wins, a bad or distant month is this month). Only a GET or a HEAD; a POST keeps its address. A filter alone on the bare path is still the bare page's twin.
- The redirect is permanent only where the address alone fixes its target. A valid `?month=2026-10` or `?year=2027` is a 308 to that period's spelled path — this month's too (`?month=2026-09` → `/ro/calendar/2026-09`, never the bare page, whose meaning moves with the clock). `?view=list` alone, or a month that is malformed or too far away, means "this month": its target changes on the first of the next month, and a browser keeps a permanent redirect with no cache header of its own, so a bookmark would stay on the month it first resolved to. Those answer a 307 with `Cache-Control: private, no-store` (`legacyCalendarAddress` returns the address and whether it is `fixed`). Refused: a 307 with a short public `max-age` for every old address — the named month's target never changes, and a permanent redirect is what tells a search engine the old address is gone.
- Static like the bare page (§549): `revalidate` the day's ceiling, no params at build, expired by the events' writes, held to Brașov's midnight. `PREFETCHED_PATHNAMES` names `/calendar/[...period]`, so the proxy gives its answer the browser's header off Vercel; the calendar's own links still never prefetch (a month nobody opened today is a render). Its canonical is the bare calendar (§342), and robots.txt disallows `/ro/calendar/` and `/en/calendar/`, so a crawler does not walk five years of months and wake the database.
- Each period is now a page of its own, so the next period arrives as a new calendar rather than the old one re-rendered: the swipe hands its step to the calendar that mounts (`arriving`, believed for ten seconds), which slides in from the side it was pushed towards, as §475 describes.

**Why the path and not one payload.** The brief offered two: a static page that carries every reachable month and renders the chosen one on the client, or one cached route per month. The first would move `EventCalendar`'s server rendering (translations, edition notes, night lines, tooltips) into the browser, put five years of events into every calendar view's payload, and leave a reader without JavaScript on this month whatever the link said, which §413 forbids. One route per month keeps the page as it was, server HTML in the first response, and is the cheaper at run time as well: a month change is a CDN answer made at most once a day per month and language, where the old `?month=` was the twin's render per press and per visitor. An idle site costs nothing either way.

**Refused.** *Not prefetching the bare calendar from the header* — one line, and it made the arrows work in the reproduction, but it rests on the router's heuristic staying as it is, any other prefetched link to the calendar would bring the bug back, and each month change stays a function. *`router.refresh()` after each push* — two requests per press. *Plain `<a>` links* — the document navigation and the white flash §166 removed. *Moving the filters into the path too* — the listing's own filters were measured working on production after the header's prefetch of the listing (`/ro/evenimente?surface=ASPHALT`, the active chip drawn), and on the calendar no filtered address is a query on the bare path any more.

**Tests.** `tests/unit/events/calendar-month-from-path.test.ts`: the segments read and built, the bare-or-spelled rule, the filters on the period's path, the old addresses, the proxy's 308 for a named period and its `no-store` 307 for this month in both languages, the header's arrows, «Azi» and chips rendered as paths, the swipe handed the arrows' paths, and the selects pushing the chosen period's path. `live-twin.test.ts`, `robots.test.ts`, `static-public-routes.test.ts` and `cache.test.ts` name the new route. `tests/e2e/calendar-month-from-path.spec.ts` answers prefetches the way Vercel does and walks the header's link, ›, ›, ‹, «Azi», the select, «Listă», «An», the next year, a direct link, an old `?month=` and a sideways swipe on the phone project; `event-pages.spec.ts` and `listing-filters.spec.ts` read the paths; the other specs that open an old `?month=` or `?year=` address (`night-event`, `partner-marker`, `seo`, and `listing-filters`' own first visits) are left as they are, so they walk the 308 as a bookmark would. `tests/unit/events/calendar-swipe-handler.test.ts` drives the swipe's own handler with a finger's events (React's hooks stood in for, since the unit tests have no DOM): a drag to the left pushes the next period's path and to the right the previous one's, with `scroll: false` and never a query; a mouse, an up-and-down drag, a short slow one and a cancelled one push nothing; and the calendar that mounts with the next period slides in from the side the thumb pushed towards, once.

**Verified.** `yarn check` passes whole (668 files, 8906 tests, 2 skipped); `yarn build` lists `/[locale]/calendar/[...period]` as a static route and `/[locale]/live/calendar/[...period]` as rendered per request. Against a production build, `calendar-month-from-path`, `event-pages` and `listing-filters` pass on both projects except `event-pages`' «changes month without moving the controls», which fails on 2026-09-30 whatever the address: the seed's events are all in October that day, so September offers no filter and the next month draws the filter button (44 px) above the grid. The same happens with the old `?month=`; it is the seed's dates on a month's last day, not this change.
changelogLine: - **The calendar's arrows, selects and swipe show the month again** — on the site a press changed the address to `?month=…` and left September on screen; each period now has its own address (`/ro/calendar/2026-10`, `/ro/calendar/2026-10/list`, `/ro/calendar/2026`), served from the CDN, and old `?month=` links are sent there. §NNN.

specsCriteria.text: Given the calendar reached by any link, the header's prefetched «Calendar» included, when the reader presses ‹ or ›, chooses a month or a year in the selects, presses «Azi», «Lună», «An», «Calendar» or «Listă», or swipes sideways on a touch screen, then the address and the period on screen change together without a full reload: each such address names the period in its path (`/ro/calendar/2026-10`, `/ro/calendar/2026-10/list`, `/ro/calendar/2026`), the bare `/ro/calendar` only for this month as a grid with nothing filtered, and a filter in the query on the period's own path (2026-09-30, `DECISIONS.md` §NNN).

Given an old calendar address with `?month=`, `?year=` or `?view=list`, when it is asked for with a GET or a HEAD, then the proxy redirects it to the same period's path with every other key kept: a 308 when a valid month or year names the period (this month spelled, never the bare page), a 307 with `Cache-Control: no-store` when it means this month (`?view=list` alone, a malformed or distant month); and a period path that is malformed, a year with a layout, or more than two years from now answers 404 (2026-09-30, `DECISIONS.md` §NNN).

Given robots.txt, when it is read, then it disallows `/ro/calendar/` and `/en/calendar/` (every period's own path) and still allows the bare `/ro/calendar` and `/en/calendar`; every period page's canonical is the bare calendar (2026-09-30, `DECISIONS.md` §NNN).

Given the calendar on a touch screen, when the reader drags it sideways far or quick enough, then the router is asked for the arrows' own address for that side (the next period's path to the left, the previous one's to the right) without scrolling the page, and the calendar that arrives slides in from that side; a mouse drag, an up-and-down drag, a short slow drag or a cancelled one asks for nothing (2026-09-30, `DECISIONS.md` §NNN).

batchLine: the calendar's period is in its path: the arrows, the selects and the swipe show the month again
